dedupe_keys.name: industrial and smallholder oil palm plantation expansion in indonesia 2001 2019 thetreemap and auriga

description: This dataset maps the annual expansion of industrial and smallholder oil palm plantations across Indonesia from 2001 to 2019. The Zenodo record says the wall-to-wall maps were made by interpreting annual Landsat composites, SPOT-6 and drone imagery; industrial plantations are large company-owned estates of several thousand hectares with linear boundaries and grid harvesting trails, while smallholder plantations are usually under 25 hectares with less regular patterns. Each polygon carries the year an area of forest or non-forest was converted to oil palm and its 2019 class (industrial or smallholder). It was published in February 2022 by David Gaveau, Mohammad Agus Salim and Husnayaen of TheTreeMap and Timer Manurung of Auriga as two downloadable zipped shapefiles (about 192 MB industrial and 280 MB smallholder), free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is Indonesia. Caveats: the maps end in 2019, mills and processing plants are not included, and the accuracy figures are not stated in the part of the record read. For simulation it gives the location and age of plantation estates, the supply base of the palm oil processing industry, for exposure of plantations to fire, flood and drought and for mill supply chain models. Related catalogue records include the mapping of mining areas in the tropics and the global cropland and crop type maps.
